title: Eviction & escalation playbook for smart routing
creator: Benji Morales
description:
Summary:
Design and implement an automated eviction + escalation playbook for the Smart Routing layer that turns real-time overload signals (429 spikes, request timeouts, elevated error rates) into safe, observable routing actions and circuit states. Goal is to keep regional/tiered SLAs while minimizing user-visible errors and avoiding cascading outages.

Objectives:
- Define a compact, versioned decision graph that maps signal aggregates to actions (soft-evict, reduce concurrency, route to fallback model variant, open circuit).
- Make decisions tenant-aware by default with configurable per-tenant thresholds and global backstops.
- Ensure actions are reversible with probation windows and decaying trip scores.
- Provide telemetry and audit trails for every actuation (who/what/why) and expose rollback knobs in Console.

Key signals (proposal):
- 429 rate: rolling 1m and 5m windows. Soft-evict if 429_1m > 3% and 429_5m > 1.5%. Hard-evict (escalate to circuit) if 429_1m > 10% sustained for 30s.
- Timeouts (upstream RTT/time-to-first-byte): soft-evict if timeout_count_1m > 0.5% of requests and median latency > SLO*1.5.
- Error-rate (5xx): open circuit if 5xx_5m > 2% AND error-heatmap shows signature across routes/variants.
- Saturation signals: GPU queue length and variant-specific qps-per-GPU thresholds.

Trip scoring and decay:
- Each signal contributes a weighted score (weights configurable per tier). A rolling combined trip score in [0,100] is maintained per (region,tier,variant,tenant).
- Decay: exponential half-life ~15 minutes (configurable).
- Soft-eviction threshold: score >= 30. Hard circuit open threshold: score >= 85.
- Probation: after action, a probation window (default 60s) prevents immediate re-eviction; gradual ramp-back with staged concurrency increases if metrics recover.

Actions and escalation ladder (ordered):
1) Local soft-evict: shift new requests off the troubled variant in-region to compatible variants or to next-tier within region.
2) Concurrency clamp: lower per-tenant concurrency token bucket for the variant.
3) Cross-region reroute: route to a healthy variant in a different region (respecting data residency constraints).
4) Model variant fallback: fallback to a compatible, lower-cost quantized variant with verified correctness tolerance.
5) Circuit open: route all traffic to pre-configured fallback routes and generate incident annotations and an urgent alert.

Safety rails and guardrails:
- Minimal two-step confirmation for cross-region reroute when tenant data residency is strict (policy flag).
- Rate-limited rollbacks and a manual override in Console.
- Canary probes before full cutover: synthetic probes (deterministic prompts) and a small probe fraction of real traffic.
- Automatic rollback if regression observed on quality evals tied to the tenant's promptset.

Telemetry and observability:
- Instrument trip score, contributing signals, timestamps of action, pre/post metrics (latency, errors, 429s), and reason code.
- Expose per-tenant timelines in Console with links to affected traces and sampled requests.
- Add dashboard: "Routing Actuation Timeline" + per-region heatmap + per-variant trip-score histogram.

API/Config surface:
- New routing policy resource: fields: thresholds (percentiles and counts), weights, decay_half_life, probation_window, fallback_order, data_residency_policy.
- CLI/SDK to preview policy impact via historical telemetry replay.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Phase 1 (this ticket, 3 sprints): signal aggregation service + trip scoring prototype, local soft-evict enforcement in router, baseline telemetry.
- Phase 2: cross-region routing, variant fallback plumbing, Console UI for policy authoring and manual overrides.
- Phase 3: rollout controls (canaries, staged ramp), per-tenant override and RBAC, SLA-based automated retries.

Acceptance criteria:
- Router respects soft-evict signals and moves >=95% of new requests off an evicted variant within 10s for controlled tests.
- Trip scores recorded and visible in Console for every actuation.
- Automated canary probes detect regressions and block rollouts in at least two manual test runs.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: false positives causing unnecessary model swaps. Mitigation: two-window confirmation + small probe fraction + decayed trip score.
- Risk: cross-region routing increases tail latency. Mitigation: honor latency SLOs and prefer in-region fallback unless policy allows.

Notes and references:
- See incident postmortem (inc-2025-01-region-surge) for example signal patterns.
- Perf notes: evaluate batching behavior when switching variants to avoid cache/kv churn.

Next steps (short):
- Sync with Console PM and Privacy/legal on data residency constraints (scheduled 2025-03-06).
- Spike: implement a scoring microservice (2d) and demo to SRE.
- Create follow-up eng tickets for probe harness and Console flows.
